steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Angular's core decorator and common module for basic directives.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'
steps.expectedOutcome: The component file will have the necessary imports to define an Angular component and use common directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the essential Angular modules needed for this component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a component class named LocalStorageComponent with the @Component decorator and basic metadata.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before class, add the @Component decorator above it, and provide an empty template and styles array in the metadata.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example component class in Angular
export class ExampleComponent {}
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named LocalStorageComponent is defined with the @Component decorator.
successCriteria: The LocalStorageComponent class is exported and decorated with @Component, containing template and styles metadata.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the LocalStorageComponent class with the Angular decorator.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the class is named LocalStorageComponent, exported, and has the @Component decorator with template and styles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create an exported class named LocalStorageComponent with @Component decorator.

steps.title: Initialize component state with typed properties
steps.instruction: Inside the LocalStorageComponent class, add two typed string properties: 'storedValue' and 'inputText'. Initialize 'storedValue' as an empty string and 'inputText' as an empty string.
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the class body, using TypeScript type annotations. For example: propertyName: string = '';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has typed properties to store localStorage data and user input.
successCriteria: The LocalStorageComponent class contains both 'storedValue: string = ''' and 'inputText: string = ''' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added typed properties to store localStorage data and user input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both properties are typed as strings and initialized as empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't have the required typed properties. Add 'storedValue' and 'inputText' as string properties initialized to empty strings.

steps.title: Create saveToLocalStorage method
steps.instruction: Inside the LocalStorageComponent class, define a method named saveToLocalStorage that saves the inputText property to localStorage and updates the storedValue property.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.setItem() to save the value and assign it to this.storedValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can save the current input text to localStorage and update the stored value.
successCriteria: The saveToLocalStorage method is defined in the LocalStorageComponent class, uses localStorage.setItem() to save inputText, and updates storedValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the saveToLocalStorage method that handles saving data to localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your method saves inputText to localStorage and updates storedValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't quite right. Check that it saves to localStorage and updates the storedValue property.

steps.title: Create loadFromLocalStorage method
steps.instruction: Define a method named loadFromLocalStorage in your LocalStorageComponent class that reads from localStorage and updates the storedValue property.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.getItem() to retrieve the value, then assign it to this.storedValue. Remember to handle the case where nothing is stored.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a loadFromLocalStorage method that retrieves data from localStorage and updates the storedValue property.
successCriteria: The loadFromLocalStorage method is defined, uses localStorage.getItem(), and assigns the retrieved value to this.storedValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the loadFromLocalStorage method to retrieve data from localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your method reads from localStorage and updates the storedValue property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't quite right. Check that you're using localStorage.getItem() and assigning the result to this.storedValue.

steps.title: Create clearLocalStorage method
steps.instruction: Inside the LocalStorageComponent class, define a method named clearLocalStorage that removes the stored item from localStorage and resets the storedValue property to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.removeItem('key') to delete the stored data and set this.storedValue = '' to reset the component's state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A clearLocalStorage method is added to the component class, implementing the logic to clear localStorage and reset the stored value.
successCriteria: The clearLocalStorage method is defined with localStorage.removeItem and resets this.storedValue to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the clearLocalStorage method to remove data from localStorage and reset the component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it uses localStorage.removeItem('key') and sets this.storedValue = '' to fully clear the data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clearLocalStorage method is missing or incomplete. It should remove the item from localStorage and reset storedValue.

steps.title: Add template structure with input field
steps.instruction: Add a template to your component with an input field that uses two-way binding with [(ngModel)] to connect to the inputText property.
steps.hint: Use the template property in the @Component decorator. Remember to import FormsModule if you haven't already, but for this step just add the template with the input field.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic template with an input field that is bound to the inputText property using Angular's two-way data binding syntax.
successCriteria: The component's @Component decorator includes a template property with an input element using [(ngModel)]="inputText".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the template with an input field using two-way binding. This will allow users to type text that automatically updates the component's inputText property.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the template property with an input element that uses [(ngModel)]="inputText".
steps.feedbackWrong: The template isn't set up correctly. Remember to add a template property to the @Component decorator with an input element using [(ngModel)]="inputText".

steps.title: Add save button with click handler
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a button element with the text 'Save to Local Storage' and bind its click event to the saveToLocalStorage method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="methodName()" on a button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click handler
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Save to Local Storage' appears in the component's template, and clicking it will trigger the saveToLocalStorage method.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with text 'Save to Local Storage' and a (click) event binding to saveToLocalStorage().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will trigger the save operation when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and click event binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button with the click handler is missing or incorrect. Check the template and event binding syntax.

steps.title: Add load and clear buttons with handlers
steps.instruction: Add two buttons to the template: one labeled 'Load from LocalStorage' that calls the loadFromLocalStorage method when clicked, and another labeled 'Clear LocalStorage' that calls the clearLocalStorage method when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the existing save button in the template. Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="methodName()" for each button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding buttons with click handlers in Angular template
<button (click)="saveData()">Save Data</button>
<button (click)="loadData()">Load Data</button>
<button (click)="clearData()">Clear Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have three buttons: Save, Load, and Clear, each wired to their respective methods.
successCriteria: Two new buttons are added to the template with correct labels and click handlers calling loadFromLocalStorage() and clearLocalStorage().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the load and clear buttons with proper click handlers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but check that both have correct labels and call the right methods with (click) event binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not properly connected. Make sure to add two buttons with (click) handlers for loadFromLocalStorage() and clearLocalStorage().

steps.title: Display stored value in template
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the buttons that displays the current storedValue using Angular interpolation.
steps.hint:
Use the

tag with double curly braces to bind the storedValue property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a property value in template

{{ storedValue }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the storedValue property value in a paragraph element below the buttons.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with {{ storedValue }} interpolation is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph to display the stored value from localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it uses interpolation {{ storedValue }} to display the property value.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element with interpolation was not added correctly. Try adding

{{ storedValue }}

below the buttons.
